ticket 2b16 comment: 'G4 suppresses EVERY legitimate peer-deletion mirror ... on any bidirectional pass, a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that target, and G4 therefore always suppresses the inbound REMOVE. The feature can never fire.' — the parent SET is the direct analogue of that ADD
ABSENCE: no test drives the collision through the real outbound differ; the e2e acceptance oracle at test_inbound_parent_clear_88d9.py:473-477 passes outbound_mutations=None
advisory.finding: The inbound parent CLEAR is suppressed by the same-pass outbound parent SET on every normal bidirectional pass, so in production the feature can never fire — the identical arbitration failure that ticket 2b16 shipped, found broken live, and reopened. For a de-parented ticket whose local parent is a bound epic (the only parent type Jira permits), the outbound differ emits changed['parent']=<remote_key> (a SET, because local_parent is truthy), and the action-blind scalar suppression drops the inbound parent_id clear that targets the same field.
scenarios: A human de-parents a sub-task/child (whose local parent is a bound epic) directly in Jira; the next reconcile pass runs both differs against the same snapshot and the inbound clear is suppressed, so the local parent_id is never cleared — the exact defect 88d9 exists to fix persists in production.
advisory.suggested_fix: Apply 2b16's corrected arbitration to the parent field: managed_refs should decide precedence, not a blind same-field suppression. When the ref IS managed and the peer lacks the parent (peer deleted it), the inbound CLEAR should win and the outbound parent SET for that ticket must be suppressed; only when unmanaged should the outbound SET win. Make the scalar suppression at inbound_differ.py:708 aware of this rather than dropping parent_id whenever outbound touches 'parent'.

This is the same test-shape that let 2b16's first version ship broken (a green mutation ledger cannot catch a wrong specification).
scenarios: A future run believes the parent-clear feature works because the unit suite is green, while it silently never fires on real bidirectional passes.
